### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. Brugada syndrome 9  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.479)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-1296072)

**Proposed mechanism:** KCNA5 (HGNC:6272) —DISRUPTS→ Cardiac action potential duration regulation (GO:0001977); KCND3 (HGNC:6275) —DISRUPTS→ Cardiac action potential duration regulation (GO:0001977); Cardiac action potential duration regulation (GO:0001977) —LEADS_TO→ QT prolongation (HP:0011673); Cardiac action potential duration regulation (GO:0001977) —LEADS_TO→ Ventricular fibrillation (HP:0001669); Cardiac action potential duration regulation (GO:0001977) —LEADS_TO→ Sudden cardiac death (HP:0001659); Cardiac action potential duration regulation (GO:0001977) —LEADS_TO→ ST segment elevation (HP:0030744). Loss-of-function mutations in KCNA5 (associated with Long QT syndrome 7, LQT7) and KCND3 (associated with Brugada syndrome 9) both disrupt the regulation of the cardiac action potential duration, leading to overlapping phenotypes of QT prolongation, ventricular fibrillation, and sudden cardiac death. While KCNA5 primarily affects repolarization, KCND3 affects the repolarization plateau, and their combined or individual disruption can lead to significant electrical instability.

**How to falsify it:** The discovery of pathogenic variants in KCNA5 and KCND3 that are clearly associated with distinct, non-overlapping functional consequences and clinical phenotypes in large patient cohorts would falsify this hypothesis. Specifically, if variants in KCNA5 consistently lead to only gain-of-function effects and variants in KCND3 consistently lead to only gain-of-function effects, this would contradict the proposed shared loss-of-function mechanism.

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanistic basis of these cardiac channelopathies can inform the development of targeted therapies that address the common downstream effects on cardiac electrical stability, potentially leading to improved treatment strategies for both conditions.

Similarly, pathogenic variants in KCND3 impair potassium channel activity, resulting in ataxia (spinocerebellar ataxia type 19/22).

**How to falsify it:** The absence of mutations in either KCNA5 or KCND3 in well-characterized patients with MONDO:0012828 or spinocerebellar ataxia type 19/22, respectively, would falsify this hypothesis. Furthermore, if genetic analysis reveals that patients with MONDO:0012828 do not exhibit cardiac phenotypes, or patients with spinocerebellar ataxia type 19/22 do not exhibit ataxia, this would also serve as a falsification. _(variant: The presence of common variants (AF > 1%) in gnomAD within the coding regions of KCNA5 and KCND3 that are associated with the respective disease phenotypes would also weaken this hypothesis.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared reliance on potassium channel activity could lead to the development of therapeutics that modulate these channels, potentially benefiting patients with both cardiac and neurological manifestations.
